title: Client SDK intake: enterprise triage rubric + prioritized request handoff
creator: Ava Patel
description: Consolidate recent enterprise customer asks around SDK language support, authentication patterns, and streaming ergonomics into a repeatable triage + prioritization flow. Deliver a ranked handoff list for Eng with clear acceptance criteria, security/release gates, and recommended implementation surface (patch vs major). Scope excludes API surface changes; this ticket focuses on client SDKs and developer experience only.
background: Over the last quarter we've received ~18 distinct asks from enterprise accounts: multi-tenant SSO integrations (SAML/OIDC), refresh-token flows for long-running streaming sessions, official Go and .NET streaming helpers, and a browser-safe TypeScript client that supports ephemeral API keys. Current intake is ad-hoc: requests land in Support/SE, then PMs manually summarize for Eng. This causes duplicated work and inconsistent prioritization for revenue-impacting customers.
triage_notes: Goal: build a deterministic rubric so PM -> Eng handoff is consistent and defensible for enterprise requests

Key pillars for scoring: customer ARR/strategic value, implementation effort, security/compliance risk, reuse potential across customers, alignment with platform roadmap (auth/streaming), and maintainability cost
Proposed scoring range: 0-5 for each pillar; weighted sum where ARR=30%, effort=25%, security=20%, reuse=15%, roadmap=10%
We will classify each incoming request into 3 buckets: Quick Win (<=2 sprint work), Planned Feature (epic; multi-sprint), Requires Security Review (high-risk; gating)
decisions: Adopt weighted scoring rubric above for all enterprise SDK requests starting 2026-03-01
All requests that score >=3.8/5 go to Eng Planning as 'Planned Feature' with assigned EPIC owner
Requests that require KMS/HSM changes, SAML metadata onboarding, or cross-tenant audit logging set security_review_required=true and require Security sign-off before scheduling

Streaming ergonomics improvements (client-side reconnect, resumable KV cache usage) will be prioritized separately under runtime-ux epic if they affect server API surface; otherwise handled in SDK repo
acceptance_criteria: Triage rubric documented in Confluence + template for incoming requests
Top 6 enterprise SDK asks converted into Epics with estimates and dependencies
Handoff packet generated for Eng for each Epic: summary, sample customer requests, links to Support threads, security flags, and example prompts/curl snippets
At least one pilot customer agrees to test revised SDK auth flow (enterprise SSO) in a dedicated sandbox
Security and Compliance sign-off captured for any request flagged as high-risk
tasks: Draft rubric doc and intake template (PM) — Ava
Run rubric scoring on 18 open requests and produce ranked list — Liam
Schedule working session with Security to define gating checklist for SSO/keys — Liam + Security
Create Epics in Linear for top 6 items and link ENG prefix dependencies — PM
Prepare engineering handoff packets with sample repros and customer SLAs — PM/SE
Communicate prioritization and next steps to customer success owners and the affected accounts
prioritized_backlog: High: Official Go streaming helper + reconnect and token-refresh pattern (enterprise customers: 3 accounts requesting; reasons: low-latency ingest pipelines; complexity: medium-high)
High: Python SDK: built-in SAML/OIDC convenience adapter + config guide for IdP metadata ingestion (enterprise: 4 accounts; compliance: high)
Medium: TypeScript browser client with ephemeral keys and CORS-safe streaming (enterprise: 2 accounts; security: medium)
Medium: .NET SDK: non-blocking streaming API + example for server-to-server long-lived streams (enterprise: 1 account; reuse potential: medium)
Low: Ruby/Elixir idiomatic client wrappers (community asks; revenue impact: low; scope: documentation + samples)
Security-gated: Managed key rotation helper in SDKs that integrates with customer KMS (requires security review and infra coordination)
UX-bucket: default client-side policy for partial-response buffering and retry semantics across languages (should be library-agnostic; consider shared spec)
